Any360 progress

How much of the Xbox 360 platform surface Any360 provides natively, whatever the title: every system call a game can import (the exports of xboxkrnl.exe, xam.xex, xbdm.dll), every CPU instruction a recompiled or decompiled game can execute, and the XDK library functions games link statically (Direct3D, CRT, XAudio...). The reference runtime (ReXGlue, stage 0) is the oracle each native function is verified against, not the goal. Known titles are sources: they say which entries matter first, and their own repositories track their own progress. Generated by tools/progress_page.py from db/ on 2026-11-05; raw numbers in progress.json. Public API names, ordinals and counts only: no game code or data.

One square per entry of the database, grouped by library and area; hover a block for its numbers, click it for the table. Native is implemented in this repository (any360::sys, any360::gfx, the decompilation rules) and verified against the reference; ported exists as native code in a known title's repository and is to be moved here; reference runs today only through ReXGlue's implementation; stub and missing do not run anywhere yet. The percentages count native and ported.

System calls

Every export the reference runtime's tables know, plus the imports of known titles it does not. Sorted by the number of known titles importing it, so what matters first comes first.

CPU instructions

Every instruction id of the reference recompiler's table (PowerPC, VMX and VMX128). reference: the recompiler emits C++ for it; native: Any360's own translation rules cover it; missing: neither. "used" is the number of occurrences in the known titles' code.

XDK library functions

Statically linked library functions known by name, with the address each title has them at (db/xdk_seed.json). The unnamed library ranges of each title (below) are the pool signature matching will name.

Unnamed library functions per title

GPU (Xenos)

What a native port needs from the Xbox 360 GPU, unit by unit: the command processor's PM4 opcodes, the shader microcode opcodes, primitive types, vertex, texture and render target formats, and the render features a renderer implements (enumerated from the hardware's own lists in layer/gfx/third_party/xenos_shader, tools/gpu_units.py). native: any360::gfx handles it and a test checks it (gfx_cp_tests, gfx_shader_tests, gfx_render_tests; the list is layer/gfx/native.json); reference: the reference GPU (ReXGlue's, Xenia's translator vendored here) handles it, no Any360 test runs it yet; missing: neither. See docs/GFX.md.

Sources: the known titles

Titles that feed the database: recompilations whose generated code is at hand (imports, call sites, instruction mix) and ports whose own minimal kernel lists the imports a game needs. They say what matters first; each title's own repository tracks how native that game is. MVP: every system call of a title except the graphics and audio ones native, so the title can run on any360::sys with only those left to the reference.

Toolkit components by stage

Where each component exists today and its state; kept by hand in layer/status.json. Stages: 0 scaffold (ReXGlue), 1 native system and graphics, 2 decompilation, 3 portable codebase.

SDK patch sets by area

History

One point per day the page was generated (history.json): native or ported system calls (green) over the ones that run on the reference (purple). Hover a column for the day's numbers.
